# CLI reference

Update GitHub/Gitea/Forgejo Actions, Go module, container image, npm and Cargo dependencies.

```
deps [command] [flags]
```

deps finds the dependencies of a repository (GitHub/Gitea/Forgejo Actions, Go modules, container images, npm packages, Rust crates, Python packages and custom-annotated versions), looks up newer versions, and either prints the changes as a diff (`plan`), writes them (`apply`), or pushes one branch and opens one pull request per dependency or group (`run`). Files are edited byte-exactly and never reformatted.

The configuration is read from `.deps.yaml` (or `.deps.yml`) in `--dir`; `deps schema` prints its JSON Schema. With `--renovate`, the repository's Renovate config is translated instead (`deps migrate` writes that translation to `.deps.yaml`). Results go to stderr, diffs and explanations to stdout. See `deps help output`, `deps help environment` and `deps help exit-codes`.

## Global flags

Every command accepts these flags.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--color` | string | `"auto"` | color stderr and the plan diff on stdout: auto (on a terminal, unless $NO_COLOR is set or $TERM is dumb; $CLICOLOR_FORCE or $FORCE_COLOR force it on stderr only), always, never |
| `--log-format` | string | `"auto"` | log format: auto (actions on a GitHub/Gitea Actions runner, pretty on a terminal, else text), pretty, text, json, actions (pretty records without elapsed time, colored, plus workflow commands: annotations, log groups) |
| `--log-level` | string | `""` | log level: debug, info, warn, error (when not set: debug with $RUNNER_DEBUG=1, else warn) |

## deps apply

Write the updates to the files, including go mod tidy, package-lock.json and Cargo.lock.

```
deps apply [flags]
```

Resolves every dependency, prints the same report as `deps plan` on stderr, and writes the changed files, including `go mod tidy` output (`go.mod`, `go.sum`), regenerated `package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock`, `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock` or `Pipfile.lock`, `Cargo.lock` updated with `cargo update`, `Gemfile.lock` updated with `bundle lock`, `composer.lock` updated with `composer update`, `Manifest.toml` updated with Julia's Pkg, `pubspec.lock` updated with `dart pub upgrade`, `MODULE.bazel.lock` updated with `bazel mod deps`, `mix.lock` updated with `mix deps.update`, `manifest.toml` (Gleam) updated with `gleam deps update`, `flake.lock` updated with `nix flake update`, `Podfile.lock` updated with `pod install`, `deno.lock` updated with `deno install --lockfile-only`, `jsonnetfile.lock.json` (and a committed `vendor` directory) updated with `jb update`, the files a Copier template update changes (`copier update`), and the `--hash` lines of requirements files (pip-compile/`uv pip compile` output is regenerated from its header command, other files get the new release's hashes from the index). An update of a pip-compile input (`requirements.in`) rewrites the input and regenerates every compiled file named after it. Post-processors run on temporary copies; a failed one drops that module's or lockfile root's changes and is reported as an error. An update a post-processor finds inapplicable (a compiled requirements file whose inputs do not admit the version, a Go module version that declares another path) is left out instead, and the other updates of its files are applied: it is reported as `skip    <file>:<line>  <name>  <from> -> <to>  (cannot be applied: <reason>)`, counts as skipped, and is no error.

A dependency with updates in several PR buckets contributes one update to the files: the newest non-major one, else the lowest major. Its other updates are reported with `, separate PR`, as is the lock file maintenance update (`lockFileMaintenance`), which only `deps run` makes.

The `postUpgradeTasks` of the config run in `--dir` after the files are written, in the order `run` uses, when `--allow-tasks` (or `$DEPS_ALLOW_TASKS`) allows each of their commands. Otherwise nothing is written and the error names the first command not allowed. With `files` globs, every other file below `--dir` the commands changed is restored to its state before them (ignored files are left alone).

The platform is only detected from CI environment variables. Locally, lookups run without a platform token unless one of the token variables is set (see `deps help environment`).

### deps apply examples

```sh
deps apply && git diff --stat
```

### deps apply flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--allow-tasks` | strings | `[]` | postUpgradeTasks command allowed to run, `*` matching any text but ; & \| ` $( and line breaks, e.g. `go generate ./...`, `make *` or `*` (repeatable); they run repository code on this machine |
| `--concurrency` | int | `32` | maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults); a Renovate file name (renovate.json, .renovaterc, …) turns on --renovate |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--renovate` | bool | `false` | compatibility mode: translate the Renovate config (renovate.json, .github/renovate.json5, …, or --config) instead of reading .deps.yaml; deps migrate writes the same translation |
| `--report` | string | `""` | also write the result as JSON to this file (see deps help output) |
| `--show-skipped` | bool | `false` | also print skipped dependencies (skip lines) |

## deps completion

Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell.

```
deps completion [command]
```

Generate the autocompletion script for deps for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

Subcommands:

- [`deps completion bash`](#deps-completion-bash): Generate the autocompletion script for bash
- [`deps completion fish`](#deps-completion-fish): Generate the autocompletion script for fish
- [`deps completion powershell`](#deps-completion-powershell): Generate the autocompletion script for powershell
- [`deps completion zsh`](#deps-completion-zsh): Generate the autocompletion script for zsh

## deps completion bash

Generate the autocompletion script for bash.

```
deps completion bash
```

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(deps completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	deps completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/deps

#### macOS:

	deps completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/deps

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

## deps completion fish

Generate the autocompletion script for fish.

```
deps completion fish
```

Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	deps completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

	deps completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/deps.fish

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

## deps completion powershell

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

```
deps completion powershell
```

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

The script registers the completer for the command named like the script file, so save it
as deps.ps1:

	deps completion powershell > deps.ps1

To load completions in your current shell session, run it:

	. ./deps.ps1

To load completions for every new session, run it from your powershell profile.

## deps completion zsh

Generate the autocompletion script for zsh.

```
deps completion zsh
```

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(deps completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	deps completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_deps"

#### macOS:

	deps completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_deps

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

## deps config

Check, show and describe the configuration (.deps.yaml).

```
deps config [command]
```

Works on the configuration without resolving any dependency and without network access: `check` validates it, `show` prints the effective values and `describe` documents the keys. `check` and `show` read the file `plan` would read (`--dir`, `--config`).

Subcommands:

- [`deps config check`](#deps-config-check): Validate the configuration offline, e.g. in a pre-commit hook
- [`deps config describe`](#deps-config-describe): Describe the configuration keys, or one key in full
- [`deps config show`](#deps-config-show): Print the effective configuration with defaults filled in

## deps config check

Validate the configuration offline, e.g. in a pre-commit hook.

```
deps config check [flags]
```

Loads and validates the config file as `plan` does, offline: strict decoding (unknown keys are errors), every value, glob, constraint, schedule and template. It prints `<path>: ok` and exits 0, or prints every problem and exits 2. Without a config file it reports that the built-in defaults apply and exits 0.

Static warnings, such as rules that can never match, go to stderr as `warn    <path>: <field>: <msg>` and do not change the exit code.

Because it needs no token, network or checkout history, it fits a pre-commit hook. With [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com):

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: deps-config-check
        name: deps config check
        entry: deps config check
        language: system
        files: ^\.deps\.ya?ml$
        pass_filenames: false
```

As a plain git hook, `.git/hooks/pre-commit`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
exec deps config check
```

For a config elsewhere, add `--config <file>` to the entry and adjust `files`.

### deps config check examples

```sh
deps config check
deps config check --config .github/deps.yaml
```

### deps config check flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults) |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |

## deps config describe

Describe the configuration keys, or one key in full.

```
deps config describe [key]
```

Without a key, lists every configuration key, one per line, with the first sentence of its description. Nested keys are paths: `actions.defaultHost`, `rules[].allow`, `custom[].checksum.asset`, `customDatasources.<name>.url`.

With a key, prints its type, default, allowed values and limits, then its full description, as plain text (the content of the [configuration reference](configuration.md), from the same schema). A key is accepted as listed or as it appears in error messages: `rules.allow`, `rules[].allow` and `rules[2].allow` are the same key, and so are `customDatasources.<name>.url` and `customDatasources.envtest.url`.

An unknown key exits 2 and suggests the closest key, or the keys ending in it (`allow` suggests `rules[].allow`).

### deps config describe examples

```sh
deps config describe
deps config describe rules[].allow
deps config describe customDatasources.<name>.versions
```

## deps config show

Print the effective configuration with defaults filled in.

```
deps config show [flags]
```

Prints the effective configuration as YAML: every top-level key in schema order, with the value of the config file or else its default (`pin: keep`, `branchPrefix: deps/`, the default `ignorePaths`, …). Rules, custom managers and custom datasources are printed as written, with the defaults of their unset keys (`custom[].versioning: semver`, `customDatasources.<name>.format: json`) added. A leading comment names the file, or says that the built-in defaults apply.

Four values are shown as the commands resolve them:

- `git.author` is the commit author of `run`: `--author-name`/`--author-email` (accepted here too), then `$DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR`, then the file, then `deps[bot] <deps-bot@noreply.invalid>`.
- `actions.defaultHost` is the host of `owner/repo@ref` actions: the file, then the host of `$DEPS_DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL`, then the platform default (`data.forgejo.org` on Forgejo Actions, else `github.com`).
- `git.platformCommit` is `$DEPS_PLATFORM_COMMIT` when set, else the file, else `auto`.
- `gitlabci.url` is the GitLab instance of the `gitlabci` manager: the file, then `$CI_SERVER_URL`, then `https://gitlab.com`.

`--sources` appends where each value comes from as a comment: `default`, `file`, `env` or `flag`. Nested objects (`git`, `actions`, `gitlabci`, `terraform`, `gomod`, `composer`, `dashboard`, `lockFileMaintenance`) are annotated per key:

```yaml
# effective configuration of /repo/.deps.yaml
version: 1 # default
pin: digest # file
...
git:
  author: bot <bot@example.com> # env
...
actions:
  defaultHost: github.com # default
```

### deps config show examples

```sh
deps config show
DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR='bot <bot@example.com>' deps config show --sources
```

### deps config show flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--author-email` | string | `""` | commit author email, as for run (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then git.author of the config, then deps-bot@noreply.invalid) |
| `--author-name` | string | `""` | commit author name, as for run (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then git.author of the config, then deps[bot]) |
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults) |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--sources` | bool | `false` | annotate each value with where it comes from: default, file, env or flag |

## deps explain

Explain the rules, candidates and decision for each matching dependency.

```
deps explain <name-glob>... [flags]
```

Resolves only the dependencies whose name matches any of the doublestar globs (the syntax of rule `names`, for example `'actions/*'` or `'k8s.io/*'`) and prints, per occurrence, the matching rules, the effective policy, the rejected candidates by reason and the resulting update. The report goes to stdout, one block per occurrence:

```
actions/checkout  .gitea/workflows/ci.yml:10  (github-actions, action, git-tags, tag)
  current   v7.0.1
  rules     none
  policy    pin=keep allow=- allowedUpdateTypes=major,minor,patch,digest,pin group=- schedule=always minAge=-
  candidates 68
  rejected  not newer: 58 (v7.0.1, v7.0.0, v6.1.0, ...)  precision: 7 (v7, v6, v5, ...)  invalid: 2 (v2-beta, v6-beta)  prefix: 1 (1.0.0)
  result    up to date

github.com/spf13/pflag  go.mod:28  (gomod, indirect, go, go)
  current   v1.0.10
  rules     none
  policy    pin=keep allow=- allowedUpdateTypes=major,minor,patch,digest,pin group=- schedule=always minAge=-
  result    skipped: ignored by default (indirect; enable with a rule setting ignore: false)
```

The header names the manager, dep type, datasource and versioning. The other lines in a block:

- `age       released <date>` follows `current` when a `currentAge` rule needed the release time of the current version; `age       unknown (currentAge rules do not match)` when the datasource does not know it.
- `builtin   monorepo <name> -> group "<name> monorepo"` appears for monorepo members.
- `rules` lists the matching rules as `#<i> match: <fields>; apply: <fields> (from <file>:<line>)` (the match fields it sets, `all` when none, then the apply fields it sets), or `none` when no rule matched, for example `#2 match: managers=[gomod] depTypes=[indirect]; apply: ignore=false (from .deps.yaml:12)`. `<i>` counts the rules of the whole config, those of `extends` first; `<file>` is where the rule is written: the config file (`.deps.yaml`, or the `--config` path), or an extended file as `<repo>//<path>[#<ref>]` (`(from org/deps-config//.deps.yaml:12)`). Rules with `updateTypes` that applied to an update follow as `#<i> match: <fields>; apply: <fields> (applies to <type>, from <file>:<line>)`.
- `policy` is the effective result of the apply fields: `pin`, `allow`, `allowedUpdateTypes`, `group`, `schedule` and `minAge`; `versioning=`, `rangeStrategy=` and `automerge=` are appended when set. It is followed by one `<type>: <policy>` line per type that `updateTypes` rules applied to.
- `rejected` groups versions by reason, most frequent first, with up to 3 newest examples each. Reasons include `ignored by rule #4 for major`, `outside allow /^\d+\.\d+$/`, `update type major not allowed`, `too new (released 2026-11-01, minimum 28 days)`, `release time unknown (minimum 28 days, timestamp-required)`, `older than current`, `above latest` (npm: a major above `dist-tags.latest`'s), `prerelease`, `precision` and `not newer`. The policy's `minAge=` reads `28 days (timestamp-required)` under `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: timestamp-required`.
- `result` reads `skipped: <reason>`, `error: <err>`, `up to date`, or one `update` line per PR bucket, for example `update v6.0.0 -> v7.0.1 (major, bucket major)`.
- Each advisory is printed as `security  <id>  <summary>  <url>`.

**Base branch.** `--base <branch>` explains a base branch as `deps run` resolves it: from the tip of origin's branch (a temporary linked work tree, unless the checkout is at that tip), with its `rules[].baseBranches` matching it and, under `useBaseBranchConfig: merge`, the branch's own config file merged over the checkout's. stderr names the base and the config files applied (`base    release/1.x  config .deps.yaml + release/1.x:.deps.yaml`), and the base's rules read `(from release/1.x:.deps.yaml:<line>)`. A branch origin lacks exits 2.

Config warnings (`warn    <config>: <field>: <msg>`) and errors go to stderr; see `deps help output`. A glob that matches no dependency fails with `no dependency matches <globs>` (exit 1). No globs, or an invalid glob, exits 2.

### deps explain examples

```sh
deps explain 'actions/*'
deps explain 'k8s.io/**' github.com/spf13/cobra
deps explain --base release/1.x 'actions/*'
```

### deps explain flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--base` | string | `""` | explain base branch \<base> as run resolves it: from the tip of origin's branch (a temporary work tree unless the checkout is at it), its rules[].baseBranches matching it, with useBaseBranchConfig its config merged over the checkout's |
| `--concurrency` | int | `32` | maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults); a Renovate file name (renovate.json, .renovaterc, …) turns on --renovate |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--renovate` | bool | `false` | compatibility mode: translate the Renovate config (renovate.json, .github/renovate.json5, …, or --config) instead of reading .deps.yaml; deps migrate writes the same translation |

## deps init

Write a starter .deps.yaml, optionally translated from a Renovate config.

```
deps init [flags]
```

Writes a starter config to `<dir>/.deps.yaml` (or the file named by `--config`). An existing `.deps.yaml` or `.deps.yml` is only replaced with `--force`. The file starts with a `# yaml-language-server: $schema=` line for editor completion: the `deps.schema.json` asset of the running release (`https://git.jakob-moeller.cloud/jakobmoellerdev/deps/releases/download/<tag>/deps.schema.json`), or the main branch's copy for development builds. Then come comments listing the managers that found dependencies in `--dir` (an offline scan: files are read, nothing is looked up), and `version: 1`.

`--from-renovate <file>` adds the translation of a Renovate config to the new file: the same translation as `deps migrate` and compatibility mode (`--renovate`), see `deps help migrate` and [Migrating from Renovate](../migrating-from-renovate.md). JSON, JSONC and JSON5 are accepted, and its `extends` presets are resolved. Settings deps cannot express are printed on stderr as `warn    <setting>: <msg>` and left out.

The written file is validated like `deps config check`; when it does not validate, the command fails with the problems (exit 2) and leaves the file for fixing.

### deps init examples

```sh
deps init
deps init --from-renovate renovate.json
deps init --dir ../service --force
```

### deps init flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults) |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--force` | bool | `false` | overwrite an existing config file |
| `--from-renovate` | string | `""` | translate this Renovate config (JSON, e.g. renovate.json) into the new file |

## deps migrate

Translate the Renovate config into .deps.yaml.

```
deps migrate [flags]
```

Translates the repository's Renovate config into a `.deps.yaml` and writes it to `<dir>/.deps.yaml` (`--output` elsewhere, `-` to stdout). The Renovate config is never modified or deleted. An existing output file is only replaced with `--force` (else exit 2).

The config is the first of `renovate.json`, `renovate.jsonc`, `renovate.json5`, the same names under `.github/`, `.gitlab/`, `.gitea/` and `.forgejo/`, `.renovaterc`, `.renovaterc.json(c|5)` and the `renovate` key of `package.json`; `--config` names it explicitly. JSON, JSONC and JSON5 are accepted. Its `extends` presets are resolved: Renovate's built-in presets from a table, `github>`, `gitlab>`, `gitea>`, `forgejo>` and `local>` presets by fetching them (credentials as for lookups, see `deps help environment`).

`deps plan|apply|run|explain --renovate` run the same translation in memory, so a migrated file behaves exactly like compatibility mode. Settings deps cannot express are listed on stderr as `warn    <setting>: <msg>`, settings without effect on which updates or PRs exist as `info    <setting>: <msg>` (with `--verbose`); both also head the written file as comments.

- The branch prefix follows Renovate (`renovate/` by default): `deps run` closes open PRs under it that it does not manage, so turn Renovate off before the first run.
- Schedules and `timezone` are kept: deps evaluates Renovate's time windows (`before 6am on monday`, `* 0-5 * * 1`) against the run time. The workflow must run inside every window, e.g. hourly; the summary lists the windows.
- Renovate's regex (`/re/`) and negated (`!pattern`) name, path and file patterns are kept as they are.

The summary line reads `wrote <file> from <renovate config>: <n> rules, <n> custom managers, <n> custom datasources; <n> warnings, <n> notes`.

### deps migrate examples

```sh
deps migrate
deps migrate --config .github/renovate.json5 --output -
```

### deps migrate flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--concurrency` | int | `32` | maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `--config` | string | `""` | Renovate config file, which must exist (when not set: the first Renovate config file in \<dir>, see below) |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--force` | bool | `false` | overwrite an existing output file |
| `--output` | string | `""` | file to write (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml; - writes to stdout) |
| `--verbose` | bool | `false` | also print the info notes (settings without effect on which updates or PRs exist) |

## deps plan

Print the updates as a unified diff without writing files.

```
deps plan [flags]
```

On a terminal plan prints the summary only and names the changed files; --diff prints the diff there too. Piped or redirected stdout always gets the diff.

### deps plan examples

```sh
deps plan > deps.diff && git apply --check deps.diff
deps plan --diff
deps plan --show-skipped --dir ../other-repo
deps plan --config ci/deps.yaml --log-level info
```

### deps plan flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--concurrency` | int | `32` | maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults); a Renovate file name (renovate.json, .renovaterc, …) turns on --renovate |
| `--diff` | bool | `false` | print the diff when stdout is a terminal too (piped stdout always gets it) |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--renovate` | bool | `false` | compatibility mode: translate the Renovate config (renovate.json, .github/renovate.json5, …, or --config) instead of reading .deps.yaml; deps migrate writes the same translation |
| `--report` | string | `""` | also write the result as JSON to this file (see deps help output) |
| `--show-skipped` | bool | `false` | also print skipped dependencies (skip lines) |

## deps preview

Compare the PRs a pull request's checkout would get with those of the base branch.

```
deps preview [flags]
```

Resolves two checkouts of the repository, `--dir` (the pull request) and `--base-dir` (its base branch), each with its own `.deps.yaml`, and reports how the update PRs `deps run` would open differ: new PRs, changed PRs (other updates or another title) and PRs no longer opened (open ones would be closed as obsolete). A PR without a base counterpart whose dependency file the base checkout failed to extract, or whose dependency it failed to look up, is reported as not compared instead of new. Lookups are shared between the two checkouts, so each release list is fetched once. Nothing is written to the repository or the forge, except the check run below.

Output lines (stderr):

```
base    <base>[  config <files>]  (with a base branch, see below)
new     <branch>  <title>
changed <branch>  <title>
unknown <branch>  <title>             (not compared: the base checkout failed on its dependencies)
removed <branch>  <title>
error   <message>                    (lookup errors of --dir; those of --base-dir prefixed "base checkout:")
check   <url>                        (the check run, GitHub)
<n> new, <c> changed, <r> no longer opened, <s> the same[, <u> not compared] (<duration>)
```

**Base branch.** `--base <branch>` (default: `$GITHUB_BASE_REF`, then `$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_NAME`) is the branch the pull request targets; both checkouts are resolved for it as `deps run` resolves that base: their `rules[].baseBranches` match it. When it is not the default branch (origin's `HEAD`) and the default branch's config file sets `useBaseBranchConfig: merge` (or `merge-if-present`), the config file of each checkout is merged over the default branch's (fetched from origin), as `run` merges the base's file over the default branch's checkout. The `base` line and the step summary name the files applied, e.g. `base    release/1.x  config main:.deps.yaml + release/1.x:.deps.yaml`. When the default branch or its config cannot be read, each checkout keeps its own config, with a warning; with `--renovate` it is not read.

**Step summary.** The comparison is appended to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (or `GITEA_STEP_SUMMARY`) as markdown, with an update table per new or changed PR.

**Check run (GitHub).** In a `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` job on GitHub, deps also creates the completed check run `deps preview` on the pull request's head commit (from the event payload), with the same markdown as its output, so it shows on the PR's *Checks* tab. The conclusion is `success`, or `neutral` when lookups failed in either checkout: the preview informs and never blocks. Only App installation tokens (`GITHUB_TOKEN` included) can create check runs, with `checks: write`; for a token that can't (a PAT, a fork PR's read-only token), deps prints a `note` and keeps the step summary.

Exit codes: 0 with no lookup errors in `--dir` (errors of `--base-dir` are reported but do not fail; lookups that failed on an exhausted rate limit are `warn` lines in either checkout), 1 with lookup errors, 2 for an invalid config in either checkout.

### deps preview examples

```sh
# in a pull_request job with the PR checked out in pr/ and the base branch in base/
deps preview --dir pr --base-dir base
```

### deps preview flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--base` | string | `""` | base branch the pull request targets, resolved as run resolves it: its rules[].baseBranches match, and with useBaseBranchConfig on the default branch the config of both checkouts is merged over the default branch's (default: $GITHUB_BASE_REF, then $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_NAME) |
| `--base-dir` | string | `""` | checkout of the base branch to compare with (required) |
| `--concurrency` | int | `32` | maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults); a Renovate file name (renovate.json, .renovaterc, …) turns on --renovate |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--renovate` | bool | `false` | compatibility mode: translate the Renovate config (renovate.json, .github/renovate.json5, …, or --config) instead of reading .deps.yaml; deps migrate writes the same translation |

## deps run

Push one branch and open or update one pull request per dependency or group.

```
deps run [flags]
```

Detects the platform (GitHub, Gitea or Forgejo, from the CI environment, else from the `origin` remote), resolves every dependency, builds one commit per group on a temporary index (no checkout; the working tree is never modified), pushes it with `--force-with-lease`, and creates or updates the PRs. With platform commits (GitHub, see below) the commits are created and the branches moved through the GitHub API instead.

- PRs whose updates all automerge (config key `automerge`) get platform auto-merge requested. With `automergeType: branch` there is no PR: the branch is pushed, and once its checks pass the base branch is fast-forwarded to it (one branch per run); failed checks open the PR.
- With `prCreation: not-pending` or `status-success` the branch is pushed without a PR, and a later run opens the PR once its checks finished or all passed (`not-pending` also `prNotPendingHours`, default 25, after the branch's last commit while its checks are still running or absent). With `prCreation: approval` the PR is opened once the branch is approved on the dependency dashboard. With `draftPR` new PRs are drafts (GitHub's draft flag; a `WIP: ` title prefix on Gitea and Forgejo, `Draft: ` on GitLab), unless they automerge.
- With `dashboard.enabled`, the dashboard issue is read first (its ticked checkboxes apply to this run) and written last.
- With `lockFileMaintenance`, one more PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance` refreshes every lockfile deps maintains (`Cargo.lock`, npm, pnpm, yarn and bun locks, `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `pdm.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`, `composer.lock`, Julia manifests, `pubspec.lock`, `MODULE.bazel.lock`, `mix.lock`, Gleam `manifest.toml`, `flake.lock`, `Podfile.lock`, `deno.lock`, `jsonnetfile.lock.json`, Gradle lockfiles, `.terraform.lock.hcl`, and the `// indirect` requirements of `go.mod` with `go.sum`) with the ecosystem's tool; it is closed when the lockfiles are current.
- Obsolete PRs of the base under `branchPrefix` are closed and their branches deleted when the base's resolution had no errors, and obsolete branches without any PR (branch automerge, `prCreation`) are deleted when no base had any. PRs to other branches are left alone.
- On an open PR, its ticked rebase checkbox or the `rebaseLabel` (default `rebase`) requests a rebuild like the dashboard's rebase checkbox; deps unticks the box and removes the label afterwards. The `stopUpdatingLabel` (default `stop-updating`) makes deps leave the PR alone.
- In GitHub, Gitea or Forgejo Actions, a PR body deps writes (creating the PR, or updating it because its content changed) links the workflow run above the rebase checkbox: the line `Written by deps in <GITHUB_WORKFLOW> #<GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER>.`, its run label linking `<server>/<repository>/actions/runs/<GITHUB_RUN_ID>`, with `/attempts/<GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT>` on GitHub for a re-run. Runs that leave a PR `up-to-date` or only rebase it do not edit the body for the link, so it names the run that last wrote the PR's content. Outside Actions (no `GITHUB_RUN_ID`) and on GitLab the body has no such line.
- With `--base` or the default branch, the local `HEAD` must be the tip of `origin/<base>`.

**Base branches:** `--base`, else the config key `baseBranches`, else the repository's default branch. `baseBranches` lists names, `$default` and `/<RE2>/` regexes over the branches on origin (names origin lacks are skipped with a warning). Each base is resolved from its own tip, with the checkout's config, its `rules[].baseBranches` matching that base: the checkout serves the base it is the tip of, every other base gets a temporary linked work tree of its fetched tip. With `useBaseBranchConfig: merge` (or `merge-if-present`) such a base's own config file is merged over the checkout's, and the log prints `base    <base>  config .deps.yaml + <base>:.deps.yaml` for it. With more than one entry, or a regex one, branches carry the base (`<branchPrefix><base>/<name>`), the log prints `base    <base>` before each base's updates, and the dashboard has a section per base; the PR limits count all bases together. `--base` overrides `baseBranches` with one base and the plain branch names.

**Token:** `--token`, then `DEPS_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_TOKEN`, then the password from `git credential fill` for the platform host. Without any token, `run` fails with `no token for <host>`, except with `--dry-run`, which uses the API anonymously. Git pushes use the checkout's credentials. On GitLab, PRs are merge requests and `--repo` takes the project path (`group/subgroup/name`).

**Several repositories** (`--repositories`, or `$DEPS_REPOSITORIES`): instead of the checkout in `--dir`, `run` works on each listed repository of the forge in turn, so one job can serve a whole organization. An entry is `owner/name`, or `owner/<glob>` (`path.Match` syntax on the name, e.g. `my-org/*` or `my-org/svc-*`) for the repositories of an organization, else a user, that the token can list. On GitLab the owner is a group path or a username and names are project paths: `group/sub/name`, and a glob matches the paths below the group including its subgroups, `*` within one path segment and a `**` segment any number of them (`my-group/*` lists the group's own projects, `my-group/**` also those of every subgroup, `my-group/*/svc-*` those of its direct subgroups); archived repositories and mirrors are left out, and a repository is run once even if several entries name it. The forge comes from the CI environment, else from the `origin` remote of `--dir` with `--platform`/`--api-url` applying as usual; `--repo` cannot be combined with it. Each repository is cloned shallowly (its default branch, or `--base`) into a temporary directory with the token as git credentials (`AUTHORIZATION: basic` of `x-access-token:<token>`, masked in the CI log), which also push its branches, and is removed afterwards. Its own `.deps.yaml` applies, or the `--config` file for all of them; datasources are shared, so a release list is fetched once for all repositories. Each repository starts with a `repository <owner/name>` line and ends with its own summary and counts line; a repository that fails (clone, config or run errors) does not stop the others, and the run ends with `<n> repositories, <m> failed` (exit 1 when `m` is not 0). In a multi-repository run annotations name the repository instead of a file, and `--report`, the step outputs and the step summary cover all repositories (see `deps help output`). The token needs write access to every repository.

**Author precedence:** an explicitly set `--author-name`/`--author-email`, then `$DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR`, then the config key `git.author`, then the defaults. Each field is resolved separately. An invalid `DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR` exits 2. Platform commits ignore it: GitHub authors them as the token's account.

**Platform commits** (config key `git.platformCommit`, overridden by `$DEPS_PLATFORM_COMMIT`; `auto`, `enabled` or `disabled`): on GitHub, deps uploads the changed files as blobs, creates tree and commit through the REST API on top of the base, and moves the branch with the GraphQL `updateRefs` mutation, compare-and-swap against the tip listed at the start of the run (`stale info` if it moved). GitHub signs commits created with a GitHub App installation token (`ghs_…`, including `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so they show as verified, authored by the App's bot; with other tokens they stay unsigned (warned). `auto` enables them for an App token without a signing key. `enabled` on Gitea/Forgejo, or together with a signing key, exits 2; without a token (`--dry-run`) it falls back to git. Logged at info as `platform commits author=<name> <email>`. A branch tip GitHub links to the token's account, or with the configured git author, counts as deps' own.

**Post-upgrade tasks** (config key `rules[].postUpgradeTasks`) run only when a pattern of `--allow-tasks` (repeatable; `$DEPS_ALLOW_TASKS`, one per line) matches each command whole: `--allow-tasks 'go generate ./...'`, `--allow-tasks 'make *'`, `--allow-tasks '*'`. `*` matches any text except command chaining and substitution (`;`, `&`, `|`, backticks, `$(`, line breaks), so `make *` allows `make docs` but not `make docs; curl …` or `make $(id)`; operators written in the pattern match literally (`echo * >> deps.txt`), and the pattern `*` alone allows every command. Otherwise the group fails before anything runs, naming the command. After the post-processors, each group's commands (once per update with `executionMode: update`, then the branch-mode ones) run in a temporary copy of the work tree holding its changes, which is a throwaway git repository of the base (git works in it; nothing it writes reaches the checkout's repository), and every file below `--dir` they add, change or delete that `.gitignore` does not ignore (and the task's `files` globs match, if set) joins the commit. Submodule content never does, and moving a submodule's HEAD fails the group, as does a failing command. They run repository code; see `docs/ci.md`.

**Commit signing:** with `--signing-key` (or `$DEPS_SIGNING_KEY`), every commit deps creates is signed. The value is the private key itself, as a CI secret holds it, or the path of a file holding it; the format is detected from the armor header:

- `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----`: SSH signature (`gpg.format=ssh`) with a `0600` temporary copy of the key; needs `ssh-keygen`.
- `-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----`: OpenPGP signature; the key is imported once into a temporary `GNUPGHOME`; needs `gpg`.

Only keys without a passphrase are supported; a protected key fails before any work is done. The temporary key material is removed when `run` exits, also on errors and on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The key is logged at info by fingerprint only, as `commit signing format=ssh|openpgp key=<fingerprint>`. A value that is neither format nor a readable file exits 2; a missing `ssh-keygen`/`gpg` exits 1. The forge shows the signature as verified only when the committer (`git.author`) is the key owner's verified email. Without a key, git's own configuration applies (`commit.gpgSign` and `user.signingKey` of the checkout).

**Trigger:** cron triggers in `schedule` (crons with a fixed minute) are matched against what started the run, not against the clock: `--trigger-schedule`, then `$DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE`, then `$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` with the `schedule` field of the payload at `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`. `workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch` and local runs without CI variables match every trigger. Every other event (`push`, `issues`, `workflow_run`, …) is a maintenance run outside every trigger: only groups without a schedule (and security updates) get new PRs; open PRs are refreshed per `updateNotScheduled`; dashboard checkboxes still act. The value of `--trigger-schedule` is validated as a 5-field cron; an invalid one exits 2.

**Time windows** in `schedule` (`before 6am on monday`, crons with minute `*`) are evaluated against the run time in the config's `timezone`, whatever the event: `--schedule-time` (RFC 3339, e.g. `2026-11-09T05:30:00+01:00`), then `$DEPS_SCHEDULE_TIME`, then now; an invalid value exits 2. Logged at info as `trigger event=<event> cron=<cron> time=<RFC 3339>`.

**New-PR limit:** the minimum of `--max-new-prs` and the room left below `prConcurrentLimit`/`prHourlyLimit`, counting only the non-zero ones. Existing PRs are always updated.

**PR statuses** (the `pr` lines, see `deps help output`; for a group without a PR, branch automerge or waiting for `prCreation`, they describe its branch):

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `created` | new PR, or new branch (branch automerge, `prCreation`) |
| `updated` | content changed or the PR was unmergeable; force-pushed and PR edited. A branch automerge branch is also rebuilt when the base moved |
| `rebased` | unchanged content rebuilt on a moved base (`rebaseWhen: behind-base-branch`), or on request (the PR's rebase checkbox or `rebaseLabel`, or the dashboard) |
| `up-to-date` | nothing to do |
| `closed` | obsolete PR closed and branch deleted |
| `deleted` | obsolete branch without a PR deleted (branch automerge, `prCreation`) |
| `would-create`, `would-update`, `would-rebase` | `--dry-run` |
| `skipped: closed PR for this version` | an unmerged closed PR has the same branch and title, or the same versions of a major update (the dashboard's recreate checkbox overrides it) |
| `skipped: closed PR for this major` | an unmerged closed PR of the same major branch (`-major`, `-v<N>`) targeted the same majors: closing a major PR ignores that major until the next one (the dashboard's recreate checkbox overrides it) |
| `skipped: awaiting dashboard approval` | the group needs `dashboardApproval` and has no PR or branch yet: listed under *Pending approval* on the dashboard, whose create checkbox approves it |
| `skipped: outside schedule` | the run was triggered by a cron that is not in the group's `schedule`, or by another event, and no time window of it contains the run time (the dashboard's create checkbox overrides it) |
| `skipped: new PR limit reached` | a PR limit is exhausted (dashboard checkboxes override it) |
| `skipped: branch modified by someone else` | the branch tip's author is neither the bot nor in `git.ignoredAuthors` (a rebase request discards those commits) |
| `skipped: stop-updating label` | the open PR has the `stopUpdatingLabel`: not pushed, rebased or closed as obsolete |

**Automerge outcomes** (appended to the PR status, e.g. `created, automerge`):

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `automerge` | platform auto-merge requested (or already scheduled); the forge merges once required checks pass |
| `automerge enabled` | GitHub (`auto_merge`) or GitLab (`merge_when_pipeline_succeeds`) reports auto-merge enabled already, and this run did not push the branch (a push cancels it on GitLab); not requested again |
| `automerge pending` | Gitea/Forgejo cannot schedule it yet (mergeability check of a fresh push still running), or GitLab refused it for now (draft, conflicts, failed or missing required pipeline, approvals, head moved); the next run asks again |
| `automerge waiting for checks` | GitHub will not auto-merge (auto-merge disallowed, or nothing to wait for) and the PR is not mergeable yet or its statuses/check runs are not all green; the next run checks again |
| `merged` | merged directly: the GitHub fallback (mergeable with all statuses and check runs green), or a branch automerge branch fast-forwarded into the base and deleted |
| `branch automerge waiting for checks` | branch automerge: the branch has no PR and its checks have not finished or none are reported; the next run checks again |
| `branch automerge next run` | branch automerge: the checks passed, but another branch was merged in this run or the base moved; the next run rebases or merges it |
| `would-automerge` | `--dry-run` |

**PR creation outcomes** (appended to the status of a branch without a PR under `prCreation: not-pending`, `status-success` or `approval`, e.g. `created, PR waiting for checks`):

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PR waiting for checks` | the branch's checks have not finished or none are reported; the next run checks again |
| `PR waiting for green checks` | `status-success`: a check failed; the PR is opened once they all pass, or when ticked on the dashboard |
| `PR waiting for approval` | `approval`: the PR is opened once the branch is ticked under *Pending approval* on the dashboard |

**Dashboard statuses** (the `dashboard` line): `created`, `updated`, `up-to-date` (body unchanged, not edited), `would-create`, `would-update` (`--dry-run`), and `skipped: issues disabled` (the repository has no issue tracker; not an error).

### deps run examples

```sh
# what would happen, without a token and without writes
deps run --dry-run --show-skipped
# what the run triggered by the Sunday cron would do
deps run --dry-run --trigger-schedule '0 0 * * 0'
# what a run on Monday 05:30 UTC would do with schedule time windows
deps run --dry-run --schedule-time 2026-11-09T05:30:00Z
# in CI (the action runs this with DEPS_TOKEN set)
DEPS_TOKEN=$TOKEN deps run --show-skipped --log-level info
```

### deps run flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--allow-tasks` | strings | `[]` | postUpgradeTasks command allowed to run, `*` matching any text but ; & \| ` $( and line breaks, e.g. `go generate ./...`, `make *` or `*` (repeatable); they run repository code on this machine |
| `--api-url` | string | `""` | API base URL (default: detected) |
| `--author-email` | string | `""` | commit author email (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then git.author of the config, then deps-bot@noreply.invalid) |
| `--author-name` | string | `""` | commit author name (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then git.author of the config, then deps[bot]) |
| `--base` | string | `""` | base branch, overriding baseBranches of the config (default: baseBranches, else the repository's default branch) |
| `--concurrency` | int | `32` | maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults); a Renovate file name (renovate.json, .renovaterc, …) turns on --renovate |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--dry-run` | bool | `false` | report what would change without pushing or calling write APIs (no PR, merge or issue writes); works without a token |
| `--max-new-prs` | int | `10` | maximum number of pull requests to create per run (0 = unlimited) |
| `--platform` | string | `"auto"` | forge type: auto\|github\|gitea\|forgejo\|gitlab (auto: from the CI environment, else the origin remote) |
| `--renovate` | bool | `false` | compatibility mode: translate the Renovate config (renovate.json, .github/renovate.json5, …, or --config) instead of reading .deps.yaml; deps migrate writes the same translation |
| `--repo` | string | `""` | repository owner/name, or the GitLab project path (default: detected) |
| `--report` | string | `""` | also write the result as JSON to this file (see deps help output) |
| `--repositories` | strings | `[]` | run on these repositories one after another instead of the checkout in --dir, each cloned into a temporary directory with the token: owner/name, or owner/\<glob> (e.g. `my-org/*`, `my-org/svc-*`) for the repositories of an organization or user the token can list (GitLab: group/sub/name, a glob covers subgroups, \*\* any number of path segments), without archived ones and mirrors (repeatable, comma-separated) |
| `--schedule-time` | string | `""` | evaluate schedule time windows at this RFC 3339 time instead of now, e.g. 2026-11-09T05:30:00+01:00 |
| `--show-skipped` | bool | `false` | also print skipped dependencies (skip lines) |
| `--signing-key` | string | `""` | sign deps' commits with this passphrase-less private key (OpenSSH or armored OpenPGP), given as the key itself or a file path (when not set: unsigned) |
| `--token` | string | `""` | platform API token; git pushes use the checkout's credentials (when not set: $GITHUB_TOKEN, $GITEA_TOKEN, $FORGEJO_TOKEN, $GITLAB_TOKEN, then the git credential helper) |
| `--trigger-schedule` | string | `""` | act as if the run was triggered by this workflow cron, overriding $GITHUB_EVENT_NAME/$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH |

## deps schema

Print the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of .deps.yaml.

```
deps schema
```

Prints the JSON Schema of `.deps.yaml`, reflected from the config types, with every key's description (`markdownDescription` holds the long form editors show on hover). Unknown keys are rejected (`additionalProperties: false`), as in the loader. The repository's `deps.schema.json` is this output. `$id` is the schema's URL for this version: the `deps.schema.json` asset of the release (`dev` builds: the file on main).

### deps schema examples

```sh
deps schema > deps.schema.json
# then start .deps.yaml with the schema of your deps version (`deps version`):
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://git.jakob-moeller.cloud/jakobmoellerdev/deps/releases/download/<version>/deps.schema.json
```

## deps submit

Submit the dependencies to GitHub's dependency graph.

```
deps submit [flags]
```

Extracts every dependency (no lookups, no network apart from the submission) and submits them to GitHub's dependency graph as one snapshot (the [dependency submission API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/dependency-submission)): one manifest per file, one package URL per dependency. GitHub then shows them in *Insights → Dependency graph*, includes them in the SBOM export and in dependency review, and raises Dependabot alerts for the ecosystems of its advisory database.

**What is submitted.** By default only the files GitHub does not read by itself: Gradle builds and version catalogs, the Maven and Gradle wrappers, Dockerfiles, Compose files, Kubernetes and Helm YAML and other image references, custom (annotation and regex) dependencies, and the other managers whose datasource has a package URL type. go.mod, package.json, the Python manifests, Cargo.toml, pom.xml and workflows are left out, because GitHub parses them itself (with the full resolved graph for Go and Python) and a submitted manifest replaces GitHub's view of that file; `--all-managers` submits them too.

**Package URLs** by datasource: `go` → `pkg:golang/<module>`, `npm` → `pkg:npm/<name>` (`%40scope/name`), `pypi` → `pkg:pypi/<name>`, `crate` → `pkg:cargo/<name>`, `maven` → `pkg:maven/<group>/<artifact>`, `github-releases` (github.com) → `pkg:github/<owner>/<repo>`, `docker` → `pkg:docker/<path>` (with `?repository_url=<registry>` outside Docker Hub), GitHub Actions → `pkg:githubactions/<owner>/<repo>`; the version is the locked one when a lockfile has it, else the one written. Deps without a concrete version (ranges, variables, templates) and datasources without a purl type (helm, terraform, node and Go toolchain versions, git tags) are left out. Deps ignored by policy (ignored by default, or by a rule) are real dependencies and are submitted. Every dependency is `direct`; `devDependencies`, dev groups and `test` deps have scope `development`, the rest `runtime`.

**Snapshot fields**: manifest names and `source_location` are paths from the repository root, also with `--dir` in a subdirectory; `job.correlator` is `<GITHUB_WORKFLOW> <GITHUB_JOB> deps`, followed by the subdirectory path for such a `--dir` (`... deps services/api`), so each workflow job and directory keeps its own latest snapshot; `job.id` is `GITHUB_RUN_ID`; `sha` and `ref` are `GITHUB_SHA` and `GITHUB_REF`; the detector is `deps` with its version.

The token needs `contents: write` (`GITHUB_TOKEN` works). Outside GitHub Actions, and on Gitea and Forgejo, `submit` exits 2; `--dry-run` prints the snapshot as JSON to stdout instead, anywhere.

Output lines (stderr): `manifest  <file>  <count>` per manifest, `submitted <result>` (`SUCCESS`, or `ACCEPTED` when GitHub queues it), `error   <message>` per file that failed to parse, and `<n> dependencies in <m> manifests, <e> errors`.

### deps submit examples

```sh
# in a GitHub Actions job with contents: write
deps submit
# print the snapshot instead of submitting it
deps submit --dry-run > snapshot.json
```

### deps submit flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all-managers` | bool | `false` | also submit the manifests GitHub reads by itself (go.mod, package.json, Python, Cargo, pom.xml, workflows); a submitted manifest replaces GitHub's own view of that file |
| `--concurrency` | int | `32` | maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (when not set: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults); a Renovate file name (renovate.json, .renovaterc, …) turns on --renovate |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--dry-run` | bool | `false` | print the snapshot JSON to stdout instead of submitting it; works outside GitHub Actions |
| `--renovate` | bool | `false` | compatibility mode: translate the Renovate config (renovate.json, .github/renovate.json5, …, or --config) instead of reading .deps.yaml; deps migrate writes the same translation |

## deps version

Print the deps version.

```
deps version
```

Prints the version set at build time with `-ldflags "-X main.version=<v>"` (`dev` otherwise). Release binaries print their tag, e.g. `v0.1.0`; the action prints it after download.

## Environment

Environment variables deps reads. Also shown by `deps help environment`.

Every flag reads its value from `DEPS_<FLAG>` (the flag name in upper case, `-` as `_`: `--max-new-prs` is `DEPS_MAX_NEW_PRS`) when it is not given on the command line; an invalid value exits 2 naming the variable. Those variables are listed after the others.

| Variable | Used by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DEPS_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_TOKEN` | all | platform token, first non-empty wins; `run --token` takes precedence. `run` falls back to `git credential fill` for the platform host, and without any token fails with `no token for <host>` (except `--dry-run`). Sent to the platform host's lookups as Basic `x-access-token:<token>` (`oauth2:<token>` on GitLab; the `gitlab-releases` and `gitlab-tags` API lookups send it as `Authorization: Bearer`). |
| `DEPS_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` | all | token for github.com lookups when the platform is not github.com (avoids anonymous rate limits for actions and releases hosted on GitHub). Without it (and without a github.com platform token), deps asks the GitHub CLI once, at the first github.com lookup: `gh auth token --hostname github.com` (your `gh auth login`, or `GH_TOKEN`), when `gh` is on `PATH` |
| `DEPS_DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL` | all | default host of `owner/repo@ref` actions (hostname, or a URL whose host is used); overridden by the config key `actions.defaultHost` |
| `DEPS_GITLAB_TOKEN` | `gitlabci` manager, `git-tags`, `gitlab-releases`, `gitlab-tags` datasources | token for the GitLab instance's host (see `CI_SERVER_URL`), sent as Basic `oauth2:<token>` (`Authorization: Bearer` to the GitLab API); a platform token for the same host takes precedence |
| `CI_SERVER_URL`, `CI_SERVER_HOST`, `CI_JOB_TOKEN` | `gitlabci` manager, `git-tags`, `gitlab-releases`, `gitlab-tags` datasources | set by GitLab CI. `CI_SERVER_URL` is the GitLab instance URL unless the config key `gitlabci.url` sets one (else the server of a GitLab platform `run` detected from the remote, else `https://gitlab.com`). Without `DEPS_GITLAB_TOKEN`, `CI_JOB_TOKEN` is sent as Basic `gitlab-ci-token:<token>` (`JOB-TOKEN` to the GitLab API) when `CI_SERVER_HOST` (else `CI_SERVER_URL`'s host) is the instance's host. |
| `GITLAB_CI`, `CI_API_V4_URL`, `CI_PROJECT_PATH` | all | set by GitLab CI: `GITLAB_CI=true` makes GitLab the platform, with `CI_SERVER_URL` as server, `CI_API_V4_URL` as API (default `<server>/api/v4`) and `CI_PROJECT_PATH` as repository |
| `DEPS_NODE_DIST_URL` | `node-version` datasource | base URL of a nodejs.org `dist` mirror (default `https://nodejs.org/dist`) |
| `TF_TOKEN_<host>` | `terraform-provider`, `terraform-module` datasources | registry token sent as `Authorization: Bearer` to `<host>` (dots as `_`, hyphens as `__`, e.g. `TF_TOKEN_app_terraform_io`), as the Terraform CLI reads it; takes precedence over the CLI config |
| `TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE`, `TERRAFORM_CONFIG` | `terraform-provider`, `terraform-module` datasources | Terraform CLI config read for registry `credentials` blocks and the `credentials_helper`, replacing `~/.terraformrc` (`%APPDATA%/terraform.rc`); when set, the `*.tfrc`/`*.tfrc.json` files of `~/.terraform.d` (`credentials.tfrc.json`) are not read. `TERRAFORM_CONFIG` is the legacy name |
| `HOME`, `APPDATA` (Windows) | `terraform-provider`, `terraform-module` datasources | where the Terraform CLI config, `credentials.tfrc.json` and credentials helpers (`.terraform.d/plugins`) are found |
| `TG_TF_DEFAULT_REGISTRY_HOST` | `terragrunt` manager | registry host of `tfr:///…` sources without one, as Terragrunt reads it; takes precedence over the config key `terraform.defaultRegistry` (default `registry.terraform.io`) |
| `DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR` | `run` | commit author `Name <email>`; between the `--author-*` flags and the config key `git.author`; ignored for platform commits |
| `DEPS_ALLOW_TASKS` | `apply`, `run` | default of `--allow-tasks`: the `postUpgradeTasks` commands that may run (repository code), one pattern per line, `*` matching any text without `;`, `&`, `|`, backticks, `$(` or line breaks (`go generate ./...`, `make *`; `*` alone allows everything). Commands get the environment without `DEPS_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_TOKEN`, `DEPS_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN`, `DEPS_GITLAB_TOKEN`, `CI_JOB_TOKEN`, `DEPS_SIGNING_KEY`, and without `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` and `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, so their git uses the repository they run in |
| `DEPS_PLATFORM_COMMIT` | `run` | `auto`, `enabled` or `disabled`; overrides the config key `git.platformCommit` (commits through the GitHub API, see `deps help run`). Renovate's `RENOVATE_PLATFORM_COMMIT` |
| `DEPS_REPOSITORIES` | `run` | the `--repositories` variable: `owner/name` and `owner/<glob>` entries separated by whitespace or commas |
| `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`, `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` | `run` | run trigger and its payload (cron of `schedule` events); set by GitHub, Gitea and Forgejo runners |
| `RUNNER_DEBUG` | all | `1` (an Actions re-run with debug logging) makes `debug` the default `--log-level`; the flag and its variable (listed below) still win |
| `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `FORCE_COLOR` | all | with `--color auto`: `NO_COLOR` (any value) or `TERM=dumb` turn colors off on a terminal; `CLICOLOR_FORCE` or `FORCE_COLOR` (any value but `0` or `false`) turn them on, also when piped and over `NO_COLOR`. `--color always`/`never` ignore them |
| `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, `npm_config_registry` | `npm` datasource | registry when no `.npmrc` sets one (default `https://registry.npmjs.org/`) |
| `DOCKER_CONFIG` | `docker` datasource | directory of the Docker `config.json` with registry credentials and credential helpers (default `~/.docker`) |
| `DEPS_CRATES_INDEX_URL`, `DEPS_CRATES_API_URL` | `crate` datasource | base URLs of a crates.io sparse index mirror (default `https://index.crates.io`) and of the crates.io API used for source repositories (default `https://crates.io`) |
| `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_INDEX`, `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN`, `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` | `crate` datasource | alternative registries: Cargo's config (`$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, default `~/.cargo`, after the `.cargo/config.toml` files from the manifest up to `--dir`) and credentials (`$CARGO_HOME/credentials.toml`); the variables override them as in Cargo. A registry token is sent as `Authorization` only to its index host; without one, the platform token (for its host) and, after a 401, `git credential fill` are used |
| `PIP_INDEX_URL` | `pypi` datasource | index when the manifest names none (simple API, JSON or HTML) |
| `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL` | `pypi` datasource | space-separated extra indexes searched for every Python dep after the manifest's own; their releases are merged in |
| `DEPS_PYPI_URL` | `pypi` datasource | base of the PyPI JSON API (default `https://pypi.org`) |
| `DEPS_PYTHON_RELEASES_URL` | `python-version` datasource | URL of the CPython release list (python.org's JSON array of releases with `name`, `is_published`, `pre_release`, `release_date`; default `https://www.python.org/api/v2/downloads/release/`) |
| `DEPS_RUBY_RELEASES_URL` | `ruby-version` datasource | URL of the Ruby release list (YAML entries with `version` and `date`; default `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruby/www.ruby-lang.org/master/_data/releases.yml`) |
| `DEPS_CONDA_URL` | `conda` datasource | base of the anaconda.org API (default `https://api.anaconda.org`) |
| `DEPS_PACKAGIST_URL` | `packagist` datasource | base of Packagist's metadata API (`/p2/<name>.json`), also for composer.json repositories naming `https://packagist.org` or `https://repo.packagist.org` (default `https://repo.packagist.org`) |
| `COMPOSER_AUTH` | `packagist` datasource | Composer's auth.json as JSON: `http-basic` (`{"repo.example.com": {"username": "…", "password": "…"}}`) and `bearer` (`{"repo.example.com": "<token>"}`) credentials by host for composer repositories; `composer update` reads it too |
| `DEPS_RUBYGEMS_URL` | `rubygems` datasource | base of the rubygems.org API, also for Gemfiles naming `https://rubygems.org` (default `https://rubygems.org`) |
| `DEPS_RUST_MANIFESTS_URL` | `rust-version` datasource | URL of the Rust manifest index (one `…/dist/<date>/channel-rust-<version>.toml` URL per line; default `https://static.rust-lang.org/manifests.txt`) |
| `DEPS_GALAXY_URL` | `galaxy`, `galaxy-collection` datasources | Ansible Galaxy server of roles and of collections without a `source` (default `https://galaxy.ansible.com`; a Galaxy NG server or mirror) |

| `DEPS_JULIA_REGISTRY_URL` | `julia-registry` datasource | raw file base of the Julia registry (default `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliaRegistries/General/HEAD`; a mirror or another registry with General's layout, userinfo sent as basic auth) |
| `BUNDLE_<HOST>` | `rubygems` datasource | Bundler's credentials for a gem server (`gems.example-corp.com` → `BUNDLE_GEMS__EXAMPLE___CORP__COM`): `user:password`, or a token; sent as basic auth to that host only |
| `DEPS_CIRCLECI_URL`, `DEPS_CIRCLECI_TOKEN` | `orb` datasource | CircleCI host of the orb registry (default `https://circleci.com`; CircleCI server), and an API token for private orbs, sent as `Circle-Token` and bare `Authorization` to that host |

| `DEPS_AZURE_DEVOPS_URL`, `DEPS_AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN` | `azure-pipelines-tasks` datasource | both set: the task versions are those installed in this Azure DevOps organization or collection (`https://dev.azure.com/<org>`), listed with the personal access token as basic auth, instead of the public lists |

| `DEPS_HEXPM_BOB_URL` | `hexpm-bob` datasource | base of bob's build lists (`/builds/<name>/builds.txt`; default `https://builds.hex.pm`) |
