| `DEPS_ENDOFLIFE_DATE_URL` | `endoflife-date` datasource | base URL of the endoflife.date API (default `https://endoflife.date/api`); a dep's Renovate `registryUrl` overrides it |
| `PUB_HOSTED_URL` | `dart` datasource | default pub repository, as for the pub client (default `https://pub.dev`); a `hosted` dependency uses its own URL |
| `DEPS_DART_ARCHIVE_URL` | `dart-version` datasource | Google Cloud Storage JSON API base serving the `dart-archive` bucket (default `https://storage.googleapis.com`) |
| `FLUTTER_STORAGE_BASE_URL` | `flutter-version` datasource | Flutter storage base, as for the flutter tool's mirrors: the release list is `<base>/flutter_infra_release/releases/releases_linux.json` (default `https://storage.googleapis.com`) |
| `JSR_URL` | `jsr` datasource | JSR registry, as for the deno CLI (default `https://jsr.io`) |
| `DEPS_DENO_URL` | `deno` datasource | base of the deno.land registry's CDN serving `/<module>/meta/versions.json` (default `https://cdn.deno.land`) |
| `GOPROXY`, `GONOPROXY`, `GOPRIVATE`, `GOMODCACHE` | `go` datasource | read via `go env -json` (the process environment when `go` is not on `PATH`). `GOMODCACHE`'s `cache/download/**/@v/*.info` files provide release times without network. |
| `NIX_CONFIG` | `nix` manager (`apply`, `run`) | nix's own configuration, in effect for `nix flake update`; deps appends `extra-access-tokens = github.com=<token>` when it has a github.com token (the platform token on GitHub, else `DEPS_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN`) |
| `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITEA_ACTIONS`, `FORGEJO_ACTIONS`, `GITHUB_SERVER_URL`, `GITHUB_API_URL`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `FORGEJO_SERVER_URL`, `FORGEJO_API_URL`, `FORGEJO_REPOSITORY` | all | platform detection: `FORGEJO_ACTIONS=true` → forgejo, `GITEA_ACTIONS=true` → gitea, `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` → github; the `FORGEJO_*` variables fall back to the `GITHUB_*` ones. `GITHUB_ACTIONS` or `GITEA_ACTIONS` without `FORGEJO_ACTIONS` also makes `--log-format auto` the `actions` format (workflow commands). `run` also detects from the `origin` remote; `plan`, `apply` and `explain` only from these variables. |
| `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `GITEA_STEP_SUMMARY` | all | step summary file (see `deps help output`) |
| `GITHUB_OUTPUT` | `plan`, `apply`, `run` | step outputs file: the counts are appended (see `deps help output`) |
| `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` | all | on GitHub Actions, annotation paths are made relative to it |
| `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`, `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`, `GITHUB_WORKFLOW` | `run` | on GitHub, Gitea and Forgejo Actions, PR bodies deps writes link the workflow run `<server>/<repository>/actions/runs/<GITHUB_RUN_ID>` (server and repository as for platform detection; `/attempts/<n>` appended on GitHub when `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` is above 1), labeled `<GITHUB_WORKFLOW> #<GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER>`; without `GITHUB_RUN_ID` there is no link (see `deps help run`) |
| `DEPS_ALL_MANAGERS` | `submit` | default of `--all-managers`: also submit the manifests GitHub reads by itself (go.mod, package.json, Python, Cargo, pom.xml, workflows); a submitted manifest replaces GitHub's own view of that file |
| `DEPS_API_URL` | `run` | default of `--api-url`: API base URL (default: detected) |
| `DEPS_AUTHOR_EMAIL` | `config show`, `run` | default of `--author-email`: commit author email, as for run (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then git.author of the config, then deps-bot@noreply.invalid) |
| `DEPS_AUTHOR_NAME` | `config show`, `run` | default of `--author-name`: commit author name, as for run (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then git.author of the config, then deps[bot]) |
| `DEPS_BASE` | `explain`, `preview`, `run` | default of `--base`: explain base branch <base> as run resolves it: from the tip of origin's branch (a temporary work tree unless the checkout is at it), its rules[].baseBranches matching it, with useBaseBranchConfig its config merged over the checkout's |
| `DEPS_BASE_DIR` | `preview` | default of `--base-dir`: checkout of the base branch to compare with (required) |
| `DEPS_COLOR` | all | default of `--color`: color stderr and the plan diff on stdout: auto (on a terminal, unless $NO_COLOR is set or $TERM is dumb; $CLICOLOR_FORCE or $FORCE_COLOR force it on stderr only), always, never |
| `DEPS_CONCURRENCY` | `apply`, `explain`, `migrate`, `plan`, `preview`, `run`, `submit` | default of `--concurrency`: maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `DEPS_CONFIG` | `apply`, `config check`, `config show`, `explain`, `init`, `migrate`, `plan`, `preview`, `run`, `submit` | default of `--config`: config file, which must exist (when not set: <dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults); a Renovate file name (renovate.json, .renovaterc, …) turns on --renovate |
| `DEPS_DIFF` | `plan` | default of `--diff`: print the diff when stdout is a terminal too (piped stdout always gets it) |
| `DEPS_DIR` | `apply`, `config check`, `config show`, `explain`, `init`, `migrate`, `plan`, `preview`, `run`, `submit` | default of `--dir`: repository directory to scan |
| `DEPS_DRY_RUN` | `run`, `submit` | default of `--dry-run`: report what would change without pushing or calling write APIs (no PR, merge or issue writes); works without a token |
| `DEPS_FORCE` | `init`, `migrate` | default of `--force`: overwrite an existing config file |
| `DEPS_FROM_RENOVATE` | `init` | default of `--from-renovate`: translate this Renovate config (JSON, e.g. renovate.json) into the new file |
| `DEPS_LOG_FORMAT` | all | default of `--log-format`: log format: auto (actions on a GitHub/Gitea Actions runner, pretty on a terminal, else text), pretty, text, json, actions (pretty records without elapsed time, colored, plus workflow commands: annotations, log groups) |
| `DEPS_LOG_LEVEL` | all | default of `--log-level`: log level: debug, info, warn, error (when not set: debug with $RUNNER_DEBUG=1, else warn) |
| `DEPS_MAX_NEW_PRS` | `run` | default of `--max-new-prs`: maximum number of pull requests to create per run (0 = unlimited) |
| `DEPS_OUTPUT` | `migrate` | default of `--output`: file to write (when not set: <dir>/.deps.yaml; - writes to stdout) |
| `DEPS_PLATFORM` | `run` | default of `--platform`: forge type: auto\|github\|gitea\|forgejo\|gitlab (auto: from the CI environment, else the origin remote) |
| `DEPS_RENOVATE` | `apply`, `explain`, `plan`, `preview`, `run`, `submit` | default of `--renovate`: compatibility mode: translate the Renovate config (renovate.json, .github/renovate.json5, …, or --config) instead of reading .deps.yaml; deps migrate writes the same translation |
| `DEPS_REPO` | `run` | default of `--repo`: repository owner/name, or the GitLab project path (default: detected) |
| `DEPS_REPORT` | `apply`, `plan`, `run` | default of `--report`: also write the result as JSON to this file (see deps help output) |
| `DEPS_SCHEDULE_TIME` | `run` | default of `--schedule-time`: evaluate schedule time windows at this RFC 3339 time instead of now, e.g. 2026-11-09T05:30:00+01:00 |
| `DEPS_SHOW_SKIPPED` | `apply`, `plan`, `run` | default of `--show-skipped`: also print skipped dependencies (skip lines) |
| `DEPS_SOURCES` | `config show` | default of `--sources`: annotate each value with where it comes from: default, file, env or flag |
| `DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE` | `run` | default of `--trigger-schedule`: act as if the run was triggered by this workflow cron, overriding $GITHUB_EVENT_NAME/$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH |
| `DEPS_VERBOSE` | `migrate` | default of `--verbose`: also print the info notes (settings without effect on which updates or PRs exist) |

On a 401 without a static token, git tag lookups call `git credential fill` once per host, with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and a 10s timeout. Every `git` process deps runs has `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, so deps never prompts. npm lookups use `.npmrc` `_authToken` entries, PyPI index lookups the index URL's userinfo (`https://user:token@host/simple`), and docker lookups the Docker credential chain (`~/.docker/config.json` and credential helpers).

Docker Hub limits anonymous pulls per IP address (`ratelimit-limit: 100;w=3600` at the time of writing) and counts every manifest GET; HEADs are free. deps resolves digests with HEADs and fetches a manifest only for release times. In repositories with many Docker Hub images, or on shared runner IPs, log in (`docker login`, or credentials for `docker.io` in `$DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json`). An exhausted quota fails the affected lookups at once with `rate limited by registry-1.docker.io`, instead of retrying until the window ends.

## Exit codes

Exit codes of every command. Also shown by `deps help exit-codes`.

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `0` | success, no errors; lookups that failed on an exhausted rate limit (`warn` lines, retried by the next run) do not count as errors |
| `1` | any error, including per-dependency lookup errors and per-PR errors (already printed as `error` lines), or a fatal error printed as `deps: <err>` |
| `2` | usage error: bad flag or argument, invalid `--log-level`/`--log-format`/`--platform`/`--concurrency`, invalid `DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR`, invalid `--trigger-schedule`/`DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE` or `--schedule-time`/`DEPS_SCHEDULE_TIME`, a `--signing-key`/`DEPS_SIGNING_KEY` that is no OpenSSH or armored OpenPGP private key, an invalid `DEPS_PLATFORM_COMMIT`, `git.platformCommit: enabled` on Gitea/Forgejo or with a signing key, an unknown key of `deps config describe`, an unreadable or unparsable `--from-renovate` file, or any config error (parse error, unknown key, failed validation, unreadable `--config` file; also a file `deps init` wrote that does not validate) |

## Output

Report lines, summary lines, diagnostics and the CI step summary. Also shown by `deps help output`.

Results go to stderr (the diff of `plan` and the report of `explain` go to stdout), in fixed-width lines:

```
warn    <config>: <field>: <msg>                              (plan, apply, run, explain: a rule that cannot have an effect)
update  <file>:<line>  <name>  <from> -> <to>  (<type>[, lockfile][, separate PR])[  security: <id>,<id>]
update  <lockfile>  lock file maintenance  (lockFileMaintenance, separate PR)   (with lockFileMaintenance)
skip    <file>:<line>  <name>  <reason>                       (with --show-skipped)
error   <message>
warn    <file>:<line>: <name>: <err>                          (a lookup that failed on an exhausted rate limit)
note    go.sum changes are computed by apply/run              (plan, when a gomod update exists)
note    package-lock.json changes are computed by apply/run   (plan, when an npm update exists)
note    Cargo.lock changes are computed by apply/run          (plan, when a cargo update exists)
note    uv.lock, poetry.lock, pdm.lock and Pipfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run   (plan, when a Python update exists)
note    pip-compile output and --hash lines of requirements files are computed by apply/run   (plan, when a compiled requirements file, an input of one or a requirements file with --hash has an update)
note    .terraform.lock.hcl changes are computed by apply/run (plan, when a terraform update exists)
note    Gemfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run        (plan, when a bundler update exists)
note    composer.lock changes are computed by apply/run       (plan, when a composer update exists)
note    Manifest.toml changes are computed by apply/run       (plan, when a julia update exists)
note    pubspec.lock changes are computed by apply/run        (plan, when a pub update exists)
note    MODULE.bazel.lock changes are computed by apply/run   (plan, when a bazel-module or bazelisk update exists)
note    mix.lock changes are computed by apply/run            (plan, when a mix update exists)
note    manifest.toml changes are computed by apply/run       (plan, when a gleam update exists)
note    flake.lock changes are computed by apply/run          (plan, when a nix update exists)
note    Podfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run        (plan, when a cocoapods update exists)
note    deno.lock changes are computed by apply/run           (plan, when a deno update exists)
note    jsonnetfile.lock.json changes are computed by apply/run (plan, when a jsonnet-bundler update exists)
note    copier template changes are computed by apply/run (plan, when a copier update exists)
pr      <status>[, <automerge>]  <branch>  <title>  <url>     (run)
dashboard <status>  <title>  <url>                            (run, with dashboard.enabled)
```

- For digest and pin updates, `<from>`/`<to>` read `<version>@<sha7>`. A lockfile-only update (`, lockfile`) starts at the locked version and changes only the lockfile.
- Config warnings come first, right after the config is loaded: a rule without apply fields (`rules[1]: is empty: no match field and no apply field`), or match fields no dependency can satisfy (`rules[0].depTypes[0]: dep type "devDependencies" is not produced by gomod, so it matches nothing`). They do not change the exit code.
- Per-dependency errors read `<file>:<line>: <name>: <err>`; a fatal error is printed as `deps: <err>`.
- A lookup that fails on an exhausted rate limit (`<err>` ends in `rate limited by <host> until <time>`: a 429, or a 403 with an exhausted quota, that the retries could not wait out) is a `warn` line instead: the dependency is skipped for this run, the next run looks it up again, and it does not change the exit code. `run` still treats it as unresolved: it keeps that dependency's open PRs and branches as on any lookup error.
- The PR, automerge and dashboard statuses are listed in `deps run --help`; the skip reasons in the managers reference.

**Summary lines:**

```
<n> updates in <m> files, <k> skipped, [<r> rate limited, ]<e> errors                                                (plan, apply)
<c> created, <u> updated, <x> closed, <s> up-to-date, <k> skipped, <a> automerge, [<r> rate limited, ]<e> errors     (run)
... (dry run: <w> would change, <m> would automerge)                                              (run --dry-run, appended)
```

`rebased` counts as updated, `deleted` (obsolete branches without a PR) as closed. `<a>` counts auto-merge requests and direct merges, branch merges included (`automerge`, `merged`); the dashboard line is not counted. On a terminal `plan` and `apply` leave their counts line out: the summary headline above already gives the same counts.

**On a terminal** (stderr is a TTY) the `update` lines are left out: the summary block below lists the same updates, grouped by the PR they go to. Everything else is printed as above. Piped or redirected stderr always gets the line format above, byte for byte, so scripts and CI logs see no change. With colors (`--color`, default `auto`: on a terminal unless `NO_COLOR` is set or `TERM=dumb`, and with the `actions` format unless `NO_COLOR` is set; `CLICOLOR_FORCE` or `FORCE_COLOR` force them, also when piped) `error` is red, the rate-limit `warn` yellow, and the summary colors the branches, `<file>:<line>` (dim), the update types (major red, minor yellow, patch green, digest cyan), security advisories (bold red), the rate-limited count (yellow) and the error count (red). Colors never change the layout; `--color always` keeps the piped layout.

On a terminal (stdout is a TTY) `plan` leaves the diff out: the summary lists the updates, and a `note    diff of <n> changed files left out on a terminal (--diff prints it)` line on stderr says how many files the diff would change. `--diff` prints it there too. Piped or redirected stdout always gets the diff, so `deps plan > deps.diff` is unchanged. The diff is colored as git does (file headers bold, hunk headers cyan, added lines green, removed lines red) when stdout is a terminal and colors are on, or with `--color always`. `CLICOLOR_FORCE` and `FORCE_COLOR` do not color it, so `deps plan > deps.diff` stays a patch `git apply` accepts.

Also on a terminal (unless `TERM=dumb`), a **status block** below the output shows the running phase while it runs:

```
⠙ resolving             ━━━━────────────────  604/2450 · 3.1s
  registry.npmjs.org    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━──────  174/238 · 64 open
  registry-1.docker.io  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━────  10/12 · 2 open
```

The first line is the phase (discovering files, extracting files, resolving dependencies and, in `run`, PRs, the groups handled) with a bar of the items done, a rate-limit wait (`rate limited by <host>, <n>s`), the counts of rate-limited lookups (`<r> rate limited`) and errors, and the elapsed time. Below it, one line per host with HTTP requests open (at most five, then `+ <n> more hosts · <k> open`): its bar and `<done>/<sent>` count the requests sent to the host so far that are finished (response read to the end, or failed), and `<n> open` those still running. The lines keep their place: a new host gets the next free line, and a host whose requests are all finished stays, marked `done`, for 1.5 seconds before its line goes, so hosts with bursts of requests do not blink in and out. All bars are 20 cells wide and start in the same column, which only moves right during a phase. A narrow terminal drops the bars, then cuts the lines. The block is redrawn in place ten times a second (as one synchronized update on terminals that support it), kept below every log record and removed when the phase ends, so it never stays in the output. Piped stderr never gets it; the heartbeat lines of the `actions` format keep one line, `deps: resolving 212/308 · 2.1s · 20 open requests: registry.npmjs.org 18, api.github.com 2`.

**Diagnostics** are written with `log/slog` to stderr, filtered by `--log-level` and formatted by `--log-format`: `auto` (the default) is `actions` on a GitHub or Gitea Actions runner (below), else `pretty` on a terminal and `text` otherwise; `text` is `slog`'s `time=… level=INFO msg=… key=value` format; `json` one JSON object per record; `pretty` a compact line per record for people, `  3.55s WRN <message>  key=value …`: the time since deps started, right-aligned, a three-letter level (`DBG`, `INF`, `WRN`, `ERR`, colored with colors on), the message and the attributes (dim; grouped keys as `group.key`), durations rounded to 0.1ms below a second, else to the millisecond. Records and result lines are written whole, never interleaved. `run` builds up to four PRs at a time; the records of each PR (its build, lockfile tools, push and API calls) are held back and written as one block when the PR is done, so they never interleave with another PR's. What each level logs:

- `debug`: every HTTP request (credential-free URL), every `git`/`go`/`npm`/`cargo` process, credential-helper outcomes (never secrets), and per-dependency and per-PR decisions.
- `info`: the run trigger (`run`), the detected platform and how it was detected, the actions default host and its source (`actions default host host=<h> source=<s>`), phase counts and durations (one `files discovered files=<n> duration=<d> managers="docker 137, helm 134"` line for the walk, listing managers that matched files by count; the entries of `custom` are one manager counting each file once), and the bot's view of the repository. Where credentials and settings come from, once each: `platform token source=GITHUB_TOKEN`; `credentials host=<h> source=<s>` the first time a host's credentials are used, `<s>` one of `platform token`, `DEPS_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN`, `gh auth token` (the GitHub CLI fallback), `DEPS_GITLAB_TOKEN`, `CI_JOB_TOKEN`, `git credential fill`, `docker config`; and `read config file=<path> [datasource=<name>]` for every config file read: the deps config and the files it extends, `.npmrc`, Cargo `config.toml`/`credentials.toml`, Maven `settings.xml`/`settings-security.xml`, `gradle.properties`, `nuget.config` and `.bazelrc`. Never the secrets.
- `warn` (the default): obsolete PRs left open because the run had errors (rate-limited lookups included), a schedule event whose cron cannot be read (every cron trigger matches), a dashboard skipped because issues are disabled, and dashboard labels that do not exist (Gitea/Forgejo).

Text logs round durations to 0.1ms below a second and to 1ms above (`duration=23ms`, `duration=11.003s`); JSON logs keep them in nanoseconds.

**Summary block.** Before the summary line, a `warn    rule <where> matched no dependency (<match fields>)` line for every rule of the repository's own config that matched none of the extracted dependencies (plan, apply, run; `<where>` is `<file>:<line>`, with `--renovate` `<Renovate file> packageRules[<i>]`; rules of extended configs and presets are only counted at `info` level), then a block starting with an empty line and `Summary: ` gives the overview:

```
Summary: <n> dependencies, <u> updates in <g> PRs[, PRs: <count> <status>, ...][, <p> held back by minimumReleaseAge], <k> skipped[, <r> rate limited], <e> errors (<duration>)
  PR <branch>  <title>  [<reason>; waiting for <schedule entries>]   (run; plan/apply: [automerge; schedule <entries>])
      <name>  <file>:<line>  <from> -> <to>  (<type>[, security: <id>,...])
  Held back by minimumReleaseAge:
      <name>  <file>:<line>  <version>  too new (released <date>, minimum <age>) | release time unknown (minimum <age>, timestamp-required)
  Deprecated or abandoned: <n> (--show-skipped lists each)
      <name>  <file>:<line>  deprecated: <reason> | abandoned: <reason>   (with --show-skipped)
  Rate limited: <r> lookups (the next run looks them up again; a token for the host raises its limit, see deps help environment)
  Skipped (--show-skipped lists each dependency):
    <count>  <reason>  (<how to update>)
```

The skip rows group reasons that differ only in detail: `covered by custom match on line <n>` (and the other `covered by … on line <n>` reasons) count as one row without the line, and every `ignored by rule #<i>` counts in one row naming the rules, busiest first with their counts: `ignored by rules #56 (4), #51, #52`. `--show-skipped`, the step summary's skipped list and the JSON report keep each dependency's exact reason.

The PRs are the ones `run` opens: plan and apply group their updates the same way. Without updates, errors, rate-limited lookups or PR actions, the headline reads `No updates: <n> dependencies up to date, <k> skipped.` Errors and rate-limited lookups are not repeated; they are the `error` and `warn` lines above. Neither are the PR actions of `run`: the `pr` and `dashboard` lines above give each one's status, automerge and PR creation outcome and URL, so a PR's summary line adds only why its update cannot be applied (or the stop-updating label) and the schedule entries it waits for, and closed obsolete PRs and the dashboard are not listed again.

**Step summary.** If `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (or else `GITEA_STEP_SUMMARY`) is set, the same summary is appended to that file as markdown, under `## deps <command>`: the headline, one section per PR with its branch, status and link (run), automerge and schedule, and a `| Dependency | File | From | To | Type |` table; other PR actions (closed PRs, the dashboard); held-back releases; skip reasons with counts and how to update, with the skipped dependencies in a collapsible `<details>`; the rules that matched no dependency (`### Warnings`); the rate-limited lookups (`### Rate limited`) and the errors in full. The file stays within GitHub's 1 MiB per step, counting what is already in it: when the summary does not fit, the list of skipped dependencies is left out first, then the held-back releases, then the PRs' update tables; if it still does not fit, it is cut and ends with a note pointing at the job log.

**Actions workflow commands.** With `--log-format actions`, which `auto` selects on GitHub Actions (`GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`) and Gitea Actions (`GITEA_ACTIONS=true`; Gitea 1.26 and later render groups and annotation lines) but not on Forgejo (`FORGEJO_ACTIONS=true`, which prints workflow commands literally), records are `pretty` lines without the elapsed time (the runner timestamps every line), `INF <message>  key=value …`, colored unless `NO_COLOR` is set or `--color never` is given (GitHub and Gitea render ANSI colors; the result lines keep the piped layout, the summary is colored as on a terminal), and deps also prints workflow commands: each `error` line and a fatal error as an `::error` annotation, located at the dependency's file and line, at the file for a file that cannot be read or parsed, or for config errors at the line and column of each problem in `.deps.yaml`; each rate-limit `warn` line as a `::warning` at the dependency's file and line; `warn` and `error` logs as `::warning`/`::error`; the config's `warn` lines (lint warnings and rules that matched no dependency) as `::warning` at the rule's line; each security update as a `::notice` at its file and line; the `--show-skipped` skip lines inside a collapsible `::group::`; every phase as a group (`Discovering and extracting dependency files`, `Resolving <n> dependencies`) holding its records, a `deps: <phase> <done>/<total> · … · <seconds>s` line every 30 seconds while it runs (when stderr is no terminal) and one when it ends; and in `run` the records of each PR as a group `<branch>: <status> (<duration>)` (groups do not nest, so the PR phase has none of its own; its heartbeat and final lines stand between the PR groups). After its summary records, the discovery group lists every discovered file, sorted by path, as `  <file>  <managers>  <n> deps[, <k> skipped]` (`no deps` for a file without any, `error: <message>` for one that cannot be read or parsed; `skipped` counts the deps skipped before any lookup), and the resolve group every looked-up dependency, sorted by file and line, as `  <file>:<line>  <name>  <outcome>`: `<from> -> <to> (<type>)` per update (`; ` between the updates of several PRs), `up to date` (with `(<version> held back: <reason>)` for a release minimumReleaseAge holds back), `skipped: <reason>` (`skipped: rate limited by <host> until <time>` for a lookup that failed on an exhausted rate limit) or `error: <message>` (its first line, at most 120 characters). The groups are collapsed, so the lists cost no space until opened; other formats do not print them (`--log-level debug` logs a `file extracted` record per file and manager and a record per dependency). A token deps gets from the git credential helper is masked (`::add-mask::`) before it is used. GitHub shows 10 error, 10 warning and 10 notice annotations per step, so deps prints no more than that; the result lines are complete. Any other `--log-format` prints no workflow commands, also on a runner. With `RUNNER_DEBUG=1` (a re-run with debug logging) the default `--log-level` is `debug`; `$DEPS_LOG_LEVEL` and the flag still win.

**JSON report.** `--report <file>` (or `$DEPS_REPORT`) makes `plan`, `apply` and `run` also write the summary as one JSON object, replacing the file. It is not written when deps fails before it has a result (usage or config errors, exit 2). Fields:

- `command` (`plan`, `apply`, `run`, `run --dry-run`), `dependencies`, `durationMs`;
- `prs[]`: `branch`, `title`, `updates[]` (`name`, `manager`, `file`, `line`, `from`, `to`, `type`, `lockfile`, `advisories` as IDs; a lock file maintenance has type `lockFileMaintenance` and no versions); for `run` also `status`, `automerge`, `prWait` (the PR creation outcome of a branch waiting for its checks), `number`, `url`, `waitsFor` (schedule entries: crons and time windows) and `reason` (why a `skipped: update cannot be applied` update cannot be applied; the label of a `skipped: stop-updating label` PR);
- `otherActions[]`: closed obsolete PRs, obsolete PRs kept open by the `stopUpdatingLabel`, and the dashboard (`branch`, `title`, `status`, `number`, `url`, `dashboard`);
- `heldBack[]` (`name`, `file`, `line`, `version`, `reason`), `warnings[]` (`name`, `file`, `line`, `kind` `deprecated` or `abandoned`, `reason`; see `abandonmentThreshold` and the dependency dashboard), `skipped[]` (`reason`, `count`), `unusedRules[]` (indices of all rules that matched no dependency, also those of extended configs and presets), `rateLimited[]` (lookups that failed on an exhausted rate limit: `message`, `file`, `line`), `errors[]` (`message`, plus `file` and `line` for a dependency's lookup error, `file` for a file that cannot be read or parsed);
- `counts`: the step outputs below, by camelCase name.

With `run --repositories` the file holds the whole run: `command`, `durationMs`, `repositories[]` (the object above per repository, with `repository` set to its `owner/name`), `errors[]` (repositories that failed before they had a result, a clone or config error, as `<owner/name>: <message>`) and `counts` summed over the repositories (a failed repository counts as one error).

**Step outputs.** If `GITHUB_OUTPUT` is set (GitHub, Gitea and Forgejo runners), deps appends `updates`, `prs`, `held-back`, `skipped`, `rate-limited` and `errors`, and for `run` also `created`, `updated` (including rebased), `closed` (including deleted branches), `up-to-date`, `automerged` (auto-merge requests and direct merges) and `prs-skipped` (any `skipped: …` status), each as `<name>=<count>`. The dashboard is not counted. `run --repositories` appends them once, summed over its repositories; its step summary has one `## deps run: <owner/name>` section per repository.
